ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The original speed of the train is $108\mathrm{km/h}$. On a downhill slope, it accelerates at a rate of $0.2\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$. When the train reaches the end of the slope, its speed increases to $144\mathrm{km/h}$.

1. Find the time it takes for the train to pass through this downhill section.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The original speed of the train is $108\mathrm{km/h}$. On a downhill slope, it accelerates at a rate of $0.2\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$. When the train reaches the end of the slope, its speed increases to $144\mathrm{km/h}$. 1. Find the time it takes for the train to pass through this downhill section.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Given initial speed u = 108 km/h, final speed v = 144 km/h, and constant acceleration a = 0.2 m/s^2. Convert speeds to SI units: 108 km/h = 108/3.6 = 30 m/s, and 144 km/h = 144/3.6 = 40 m/s. Using the constant-acceleration formula v = u + at, solve for time: t = (v - u)/a = (40 - 30)/0.2 = 10/0.2 = 50 s.
